item.author: Neu, Charmaine; Furtado, Stephanie; Dyck, Rebecca; Sheikh, Fatima; Tremain, Leanne; Johnson, Denise
item.title: Early Identification of Pressure Injury: An Equity-Informed Initiative
item.description:
所属期数: Ahead of Print
出版时间: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 00:00:00 GMT-05:00

Early detection is an essential component in averting preventable higher-stage pressure injuries (PI). However, decades of clinical practice have not yielded the elimination of preventable hospital-acquired PIs, especially in patients with dark skin tones. Late detection of PIs in dark skin tones is a health equity issue. As an equity-informed initiative, an interprofessional team in a large hospital complex developed an enabler for practice to address overreliance on simple visual inspection for detecting early skin and tissue damage. The 4Ts practice enabler provides a nontechnological and practical approach for the early identification of stage 1 PIs in all skin tones by examining skin tone, temperature, texture, and twinge (pain). This equity-informed comprehensive approach will impact early detection of PI, thereby triggering expedited measures for effective prevention.
item.citation: Advances in Skin & Wound Care. 39(6):288-293, July 2026. doi: 10.1097/ASW.0000000000000475

item.author: Jiang, Meijun; Zhang, Shaoyun; Xiao, Cong
item.title: Perioperative Applications of Electrical Stimulation in Flap Surgeries: Mechanisms and Benefits
item.description:
所属期数: Ahead of Print
出版时间: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 00:00:00 GMT-05:00

OBJECTIVE: To review the roles and applications of electrical stimulation in flap transplantation, addressing its potential to reduce flap necrosis. DATA SOURCES: Medical textbooks and a literature search were conducted in databases including PubMed, Google Scholar, Web of Science, and relevant surgical journals. STUDY SELECTION: Articles were screened using keywords including electrical stimulation, flap transplantation, angiogenesis, vasodilation, antibacterial, vasopasm, inflammation, wound healing, cell migration, and cell proliferation. Articles in which the title and/or abstract contained these key words were included in the review. More than 120 journal research articles met the criteria. DATA EXTRACTION: Research highlighted the benefits and molecular mechanisms of electrical stimulation on the healing progress of flap transplantation, which underwent a full-text review and summarization. DATA SYNTHESIS: Classify and descriptively summarize the articles based on perioperative factors closely related to flap survival. The mechanisms underlying these benefits are discussed, alongside their clinical significance. CONCLUSIONS: Preoperative electrical stimulation fosters angiogenesis and new blood vessel growth, whereas postoperative stimulation aids in infection control, edema reduction, and overall wound healing. Electrical stimulation shows significant promise in improving outcomes of flap surgeries.
item.citation: Advances in Skin & Wound Care. 39(6):E295-E302, July 2026. doi: 10.1097/ASW.0000000000000474

item.author: Melnychuk, Igor; Besh, Jordan
item.title: Utilization of Autologous Skin Shave Micrografting for Treatment of Advanced Stage Pressure Injuries: A Seven-Patient Case Series
item.description:
所属期数: Ahead of Print
出版时间: Thu, 04 Jun 2026 00:00:00 GMT-05:00

OBJECTIVE: The authors present an autologous skin shave micrografting (ASSM) technique for treating stage 3 to 4 pressure injuries (PI). METHODS: Between 2024 and 2025, 7 patients with stage 3 and 4 PIs were treated using skin micrografting. RESULTS: Seven patients with 10 PIs (3 stage 3 and 7 stage 4) underwent ASSM. The average PI size was 7.2 cm2. The average depth was 0.3 cm. The average donor site measured 1.5 cm2. All patients demonstrated complete healing within 4 months. Five of 7 patients remained recurrence-free during a 9-month follow-up period, and only 1 out of 10 PIs was open at 9 months. CONCLUSIONS: ASSM is a promising modality for the treatment of select PIs and may be considered as part of the reconstructive ladder for advanced pressure injuries. JOURNAL/aswca/04.03/00129334-202607000-00004/figure1/v/2026-06-13T090907Z/r/image-jpeg PURPOSE: To increase knowledge of the application of the autologous skin shave micrografting (ASSM) technique for the management of advanced-stage pressure injuries (PI). TARGET AUDIENCE: This continuing education activity is intended for physicians, physician assistants, nurse practitioners, and registered nurses with an interest in skin and wound care. LEARNING OBJECTIVES/OUTCOMES: After participating in this educational activity, the participant will:Evaluate patient-specific factors to select optimal treatment strategies for managing PI.Apply the techniques and procedural steps of ASSM for the treatment of advanced-stage PIs.Explain the underlying pathophysiologic mechanisms by which ASSM promotes healing in advanced-stage PIs.
item.citation: Advances in Skin & Wound Care. 39(6):294-303, July 2026. doi: 10.1097/ASW.0000000000000472
